Sasidharan vs State Of Kerala on 8 July, 2025

Order 
This bail application is filed under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.426 of 2025 of Udumbanchola Police Station, Idukki,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 376(f), 376(l) and 376(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, apart from Sections 63, 63(d)(iii) , 64(2)(k), 64(2)(m) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

3. According to the prosecution, from June 2024 onwards the accused threatened the defaco complainant and committed rape on her on different occasions, and she became pregnant and even delivered a child on 20.03.2025, and thereby the accused committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard Sri. Biju C. Abraham, the learned counsel for the petitioner, as well as Sri. Noushad K. A.,
the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the entire prosecution allegations are false and a consensual relationship is alleged to be an instance of rape.

The learned counsel further 2025:KER:49839 submitted that from the prosecution allegation itself, it is evident that the victim and the accused were in a relationship from June 2024, and until the child was born, not even a finger was raised pointing to any instance of rape.
The learned counsel also submitted that the child was handed over to CW3.
It is also submitted that petitioner was arrested on 17.05.2025, and he has been in custody since then.

6. The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, contended that the victim is a 75% hearing impaired lady and petitioner had exploited her disability, and therefore, continued custody of the petitioner is necessary.

It was also submitted that on several occasions, despite the vehement objections of the victim, petitioner continued to rape her under threat, and therefore, it is a clear instance of rape, and hence, petitioner ought not to be released on bail.
7. I have considered the rival contentions and also perused the Case Diary.
8. Petitioner was a person working in the cardamom plantation of the father of the defacto complainant.
He has been a worker for the last several years and had also taken on lease one acre of property from the defacto complainant's father.
The defacto complainant has been separated from her husband for the last ten years and has been living with her child and mother.
The prosecution allegations indicate that in June 2024, petitioner raped the defacto 2025:KER:49839 complainant in a shed in the cardamom plantation.
No complaint of any nature was filed by her.
The said act of rape, according to the victim herself, continued on several days until August 2024.

sentences.text: she had not raised any objection or complaint.
After she became pregnant, also she did not raise any complaint, and a male child was born on 20.03.2025.
Even then she had not raised any complaint.
It was much thereafter, i.e., on 16.05.2025, that the defacto complainant filed a complaint for the first time, alleging rape.
A reading of the statement of the defacto complainant as well as the statement of the other witnesses and the surrounding circumstances prima facie indicate instances of consensual relationship.
However, that is a matter which has to be probed deeper by the investigating officer.
9. Though the victim is stated to be 75% hearing impaired, as evident from the disability certificate, I am of the view that the said impairment did not affect her day to day activities.
She is fully functional in all respects and had also raised her son by herself.
In such circumstances, the said disability cannot be assumed, at this stage, to be a reason for any alleged exploitation.
10. Taking note of the period of detention already undergone by the petitioner from 17.05.2025, I am of the view that continued custody of the petitioner is not necessary.

11. Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following 2025:KER:49839 conditions:-
(a) Petitioner shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the court having jurisdiction.
(b) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.
(c) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he tamper with the evidence contact the victim or her family members.
(d) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.
(e) Petitioner shall not leave India without the permission of the Court having jurisdiction.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with the law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.

Sd/-
BECHU KURIAN THOMAS JUDGE jka/08.07.25.
